newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Thai rescue package unlikely today-source.
newsitem.headline: Japan Thai rescue package unlikely today-source.

text.p: Japan is unlikely to announce its planned economic rescue package for Thailand on Tuesday, an international monetary source said on Tuesday.
"Things are under way for a Japanese package, but it is highly unlikely that it will be unveiled today," the source told Reuters.
He added that the basic framework of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) package expected to be announced by Thailand on Tuesday was unlikely to contain any concrete details.

"It's hard to believe that there will be actual numbers in whatever Thailand announces today. Without numbers, we won't be able to figure out the financial gap (of Thailand). And without that, Japan cannot decide the details of its package," he said.
Media reports had said Japan might unveil a rescue package for Thailand as early as Tuesday following Thailand's expected announcement of the basic framework of the IMF package.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya was due to explain the package on Tuesday in a nationally televised address.

Japanese government sources said on Monday that Japan would decide on a financial support package for Thailand consisting mainly of untied loans from the Export-Import Bank of Japan (Ex-Im Bank) within the next two weeks.

A Japanese daily, the Yomiuri Shimbun, reported on Tuesday that the IMF, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Japan's Export-Import Bank and Japanese commercial banks would provide a total of $10 billion to support Thailand's ailing economy.

The Yomiuri quoted international financial sources as saying the IMF and the ADB would together provide about $5 billion to the rescue package, while the Ex-Im Bank was expected to match whatever contribution the IMF made.
